t.1.27.1: Then, having received the weapons, the pure Kākutstha, his face beaming with joy, spoke to Viśvāmitra even as he was walking on.
t.1.27.2: O blessed one, I have received the weapons and am now invincible even to the gods; but, O bull among sages, I wish to learn the withdrawal of these weapons.
t.1.27.3: When Kākutstha had spoken thus, the great sage Viśvāmitra, steadfast, firm in his vows and pure, then imparted the method of withdrawing the weapons.
t.1.27.4: Satyavant, Satyakīrti, Dhṛṣṭa and Rabhasa as well, the one named Pratihāratara, Parāṅmukha and Avāṅmukha.
t.1.27.5: And also Lakṣākṣa and Viṣama, Dṛḍhanābha and Sunābhaka, Daśākṣa and Śatavaktra, and Daśaśīrṣa and Śatodara.
t.1.27.6: Padmanābha and Mahānābha, Dundunābha and Sunābhaka, Jyotiṣa and Kṛśana as well, and the two, Nairāśya and Vimala.
t.1.27.7: The Yaugaṃdhara and the Haridra, and likewise the two Daityapramathana weapons that crush the Daityas, the Pitrya and the Saumanasa, and both the Vidhūta and the Makara.
t.1.27.8: Receive also Karavīrakara, and the pair Dhana and Dhānya, O Rāghava, as well as Kāmarūpa, Kāmaruci, Moha and likewise Āvaraṇa.
t.1.27.9: Jṛmbhaka and Sarvanābha, and likewise Saṃtāna and Varaṇa, O Rāma: these radiant sons of Bhṛśāśva, able to assume any form at will.
t.1.27.10: Accept them from me, blessings upon you, for you are a worthy recipient, O Rāghava. Radiant with divine bodies, these weapons stand embodied before you, bestowing happiness.
t.1.27.11: With joined palms, speaking sweetly, they said to Rāma: "Here we are, O tiger among men; command us, what shall we do for you?"
t.1.27.12: Raghunandana said to them, "Go as you please; abiding in my mind, you shall give me your aid whenever the time for action comes."
t.1.27.13: Then they took leave of Rāma and walked around him reverently, keeping him on their right. Saying “So be it” to Kākutstha, they went back the way they had come.
t.1.27.14: And Rāghava, having come to know them, then spoke sweet and gentle words to Viśvāmitra, the great sage, even as he walked on.
t.1.27.15: What is this grove of trees, resembling a cloud, that shines from here not far from the mountain? Great indeed is my curiosity.
t.1.27.16: It was lovely to behold, thronged with deer, and exceedingly charming, adorned with birds of many kinds that sang sweetly.
t.1.27.18: Tell me everything, O blessed one: whose hermitage is this, to which those wicked brahmin-slayers of evil conduct have come?
t.1.27.17: O best of sages, we have come out of that hair-raising wilderness; this I perceive from the pleasantness of this region.
